birth.segment: The Boy Who Refused the Streams
birth.stop: Fulham, the room that is disputed
birth.date_confidence: The date 25 September 1926 is attested by en.wikipedia, 'Stafford Beer', which gives Fulham as the birthplace. Jonathan Rosenhead's obituary profile, working from a late autobiographical fragment of Beer's own, instead places the birth in his maternal grandparents' house in Putney. The ResearchGate copy of Rosenhead returned HTTP 403 and could not be read directly, so the Putney version is carried here as reported tradition. The contradiction is not resolved. Coordinates are Fulham, the version in the reachable reference source.

stops.segment: Chile: A Nation as a Viable System
stops.stop: Santiago, the knife through the slides
stops.date_confidence: The coup of 11 September 1973 and the junta's termination of Project Cybersyn are attested by Eden Medina's account at Cabinet Magazine, issue 46, which also reports that the military found the network intact, destroyed the operations room, and that an officer took a knife to each of the project's presentation slides. Beer was not in Chile on the day; the dossier places him in England, and this stop marks the project's termination rather than a personal presence. The reported request of 8 September that the Opsroom be moved to La Moneda is dossier synthesis, uncorroborated by any contemporaneous document reached, and is not carried in the campa. Coordinates are the canonical La Moneda pin.

The appointment as Honorary Professor of Organisational Transformation at Liverpool Polytechnic, later Liverpool John Moores University, and the institution's role as principal repository of his papers are given on the LJMU archive collection record page fetched in this pass; the 1989 date for the appointment comes from the research pool and was not separately confirmed. The archive states that the collection was acquired chiefly from Beer himself in 1991, with later deposits including books from his Canadian years as recently as 2023, and warns that the collection is uncatalogued as a whole and that only provisional box lists exist. Month and day defaulted.

stops.stop: Palacio de Miraflores, Caracas, the room that is never built
stops.date_confidence: Reported. stops.stop: Liverpool, the Requiem in the apse
stops.date_confidence: Reported. The cathedral's identity and location are independently confirmed, but the claim that Beer's Requiem paintings were hung in the apse and viewed in an order mapped by the enneagram comes from the research dossier and was not verified beyond it; Wikipedia's page on the cathedral does not mention the exhibition. The departure from institutional Catholicism, dated by the dossier to 1968, and the later practice drawing on Franciscan, Vedantic, Sufi and Teilhardian sources are likewise dossier tradition, not independently confirmed. Month and day defaulted; the exhibition is dated 1992-1993 in the dossier.

stops.stop: Falcondale, near Lampeter, nine sessions on tape
stops.date_confidence: Attested by the LJMU archive collection record page fetched in this pass: nine recorded seminar sessions led by Beer at Falcondale in July 1994, with transcripts covering cybernetics, philosophy, art, government, management, the Viable System Model and Syntegrity, preserved as the Falcondale Collection and made available through the LJMU Data Repository; the digitisation date is not stated. Beyond Dispute, the canonical exposition of Team Syntegrity, is 1994 per the standard bibliography. Coordinates corrected to the Nominatim entry for the Falcondale Hotel, Falcondale Drive, Lampeter SA48 7RX; the two lenses of the research pool disagreed with each other and both are about eight hundred metres off. stops.stop: Bogota, the Colombian decade
stops.date_confidence: Attested in general terms by en.wikipedia, 'Stafford Beer', which records later consulting for the government of Colombia. The collaboration with the systems engineer Angela Espinosa, the introduction through Raul Espejo and the Aston networks, and the entry of the Viable System Model into Colombian universities, public-sector reform and auditing institutions come from the research pool's geography lens citing the same article plus dossier material. No single building is attested; coordinates are city-centre. The work is dated 1990s to 2002; the year given here is an ordering choice within that span, month and day defaulted.

stops.stop: University of Valladolid, what is cybernetics
stops.date_confidence: The address 'What is cybernetics?' and its publication in Kybernetes, volume 31 number 2 (2002), are attested by the Emerald record fetched in this pass; the honorary degree at Valladolid in October 2001 is carried in the same account. Day within October not established, defaulted. The POSIWID sentence quoted here is universally attributed to Beer but the exact wording could not be pinned to a page in a primary text in this pass, the web search budget having run out before the citation could be fixed; it is carried as attributed formulation rather than as a verified verbatim line, and the sentence 'Cybernetics is the science of effective organization', by contrast, IS verified as a standalone line in Designing Freedom, chapter 1.

stops.stop: Toronto, eight months of not being diagnosed
stops.date_confidence: Attested by the Emerald memorial article 'Stafford Beer: Celebration of a Life' in Kybernetes, fetched in this pass: admitted to hospital in January 2002 with multiple symptoms, diagnosed in May with a bacterial infection, osteo-otitis, that damaged the facial nerves on his left side, with pneumonia as a complication, treated with antibiotics and hyperbaric oxygen therapy, and with aspiration problems that continued. Day within January not stated; defaulted. Coordinates are central Toronto; the hospital is not named in the source.

stops.stop: Royal Society of Arts, John Adam Street, the celebration
stops.date_confidence: Attested by the Emerald memorial article 'Stafford Beer: Celebration of a Life' in Kybernetes, fetched in this pass: a celebration of his life held at the Royal Society of Arts in London on 11 October 2002, with donations directed to the Canadian Council on Clinical Hyperbaric Oxygen Therapy in recognition of the treatment received in his final illness. The absence of any blue plaque, statue, gravestone photograph or other physical marker is a negative finding across the sources consulted in this pass, not proof that none exists; the English Heritage and Welsh listed-building databases were not searched.
